clue.text: In favour, of trial — of one mind over stand being taken

annotationWithheld.why: In favour of trial — of one mind over stand being taken (12): PRO + TEST gives PROTEST, but no reading of 'of one mind over stand being taken' yields the remaining ATION; the clue may be misprinted
annotationWithheld.clue: In favour, of trial — of one mind over stand being taken

clue.text: A duck from the river with vegetable accompaniment

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
chard is a leafy green vegetable

explanation.surface: A duck dish served with greens, caught on the Italian river.
explanation.definitionFit: A diving duck of European lakes is the bird.

clue.text: He has to confess to a little hesitation

parts.note: to own up, or own, is to admit or confess
er is the short sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A man has to admit to a brief pause in speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He has' looks like part of a sentence, but as a phrase it describes a possessor.
explanation.definitionFit: A possessor is the one who has something, so the person who has.

clue.text: Being promoted, given no leave — it's quite wrong

indicators.note: letters that are quite wrong are in a mistaken order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: it, with the 's (is) as link

explanation.surface: A worker refused time off complains that it is unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite wrong' rearranges NOLEAVE plus IT; 'given' and the 's are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising someone to a higher rank or position is a promotion.

clue.text: Putting a note in as well will cause trouble

indicators.note: the musical note is put in the word meaning as well, so this signals insertion

parts.note: too means as well, also
D is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: Adding a footnote too will only make problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting ... in' places D, a musical note, inside TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuss or commotion is a disturbance or trouble.

clue.text: Defector under instruction thanks military commander

annotationWithheld.why: Defector under instruction thanks military commander (8): CO (commander) and TA (thanks) suggest the end, but no reading of 'under instruction' gives TURN and CO + TA gives COTA not COAT
annotationWithheld.clue: Defector under instruction thanks military commander

clue.text: "Bird" printed in yellow lettering

indicators.note: the answer sits printed inside these two words, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: The word bird appears in yellow type on a page.
explanation.definitionFit: A young owl is a bird.

clue.text: Unfortunately drove over a person when fatigued

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece stands over, above, the next
things going unfortunately go wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: one means a person, as in one should

explanation.surface: Tragically a tired driver ran someone down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' anagrams 'drove'; 'over' places that before 'a person' because in a down answer the first part sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted by too much work, so tired out.

clue.text: Pay off? Think again!

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
to deem is to think or judge

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to settle a debt and is told to reconsider.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear a debt or mortgage is to repay it in full.

clue.text: Read carefully the offer made by a rival

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or read attentively
a tender is a formal offer, as in a bid for a contract

explanation.surface: Someone scrutinises the bid put in by a competing firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in a race or contest is someone vying with others, a synonym of rival.

clue.text: French article about the first wife's reception

indicators.note: the French article stands about, that is around, the name of the first wife

parts.note: le is the French masculine definite article
Eve was the first wife in the Bible, married to Adam

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece in French covers the party thrown by someone's first wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means around here, not 'concerning'. A levee was originally a monarch's morning reception, held on rising from bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a sovereign's formal gathering of guests, so a kind of reception.

clue.text: The sailor with a way in a foreign country

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
a road is a way from place to place

explanation.surface: A seaman takes a particular route while overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overseas or away from home in another land is the adverbial sense.

clue.text: Force set at odds when there's no penalty imposed

indicators.note: being at odds means out of agreement, so the letters of these words are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A police force is divided over a case where nobody gets punished.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off without punishment is the idiom's meaning, so unpunished.

clue.text: Put off the track as Her Majesty enters parliament

indicators.note: the royal abbreviation goes into the word for parliament, so this verb signals insertion

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch's arrival at the state opening throws proceedings off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parliament' suggests Westminster, but here it is the Irish one in Dublin; ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the crossword's Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a train leave the rails, or figuratively to throw a plan off course.

clue.text: Desert island lake leading to sound

parts.note: to rat is to desert one's side
Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A deserted island with a lake leads on to a sea channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like a noun or adjective, but it is the verb to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound in the sense of sane and reasoned, as in sound judgement.

clue.text: Perhaps a bed-sit by the Avon that's barely used?

parts.note: Bath is the English spa city standing on the River Avon
a bed-sit is one example of a room, a single rented room for living and sleeping

explanation.surface: An estate agent asks whether a riverside flat in Somerset is hardly ever occupied.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a city in south-west England on the River Avon. The definition is playful: 'barely used' means used by people who are bare, i.e. undressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A room for washing is where people are naked, so used while bare.

clue.text: Capital growth arrangement

parts.note: capital means head, so the growth on the head is what is arranged, not money

explanation.surface: A financial plan for growing an investment.
explanation.walkthrough: The financial reading of capital growth misleads: capital is the head, its growth what sprouts from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A coiffure is the way the growth on someone's head is dressed or cut.

clue.text: Express dissatisfaction by returning fish

indicators.note: the word for by comes back, read in the opposite direction

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone complains when a fish is brought back.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold or criticise someone shows disapproval.

clue.text: A Greek character can always make one rebel

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
a tin is a can for food
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A Greek figure can always turn someone into a revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rises against authority, especially sailors against officers, is a rebel.

clue.text: Locomotive for a place in Alabama

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, able to move about
a port city on the Gulf coast of Alabama

explanation.surface: A railway engine is put in for a town in the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: able to move, as locomotive means, and the Gulf of Mexico port in that US state.

clue.text: Nap raised by accident

parts.note: nap is the raised surface of fabric, also called pile
up means lifted or raised

explanation.surface: A doze is interrupted by some mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash involving several vehicles is a road accident.

clue.text: Make a donation here and now

definitions.meaning: to give formally, as a gift
the current time, as opposed to past or future

explanation.surface: Someone urges giving to charity immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to hand over as a gift, and existing at this moment.

clue.text: A trousers favoured by gardeners

definitions.meaning: loose baggy women's trousers gathered at the knee, named after Amelia Bloomer
plants that flower well are what a gardener prizes

explanation.surface: Some baggy garment is popular with people who tend the flowerbeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: baggy knickerbockers worn by women, and plants that produce flowers, which gardeners like.

clue.text: Individual with gold and a landed estate

parts.note: a man is an individual person
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A person with wealth and land of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: A lord's land with its house is a country estate.

clue.text: A horse may run free on the beach

indicators.note: letters allowed to run free scatter and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A horse is allowed to gallop loose along the sands.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on land by the sea rather than afloat means on the shore.

clue.text: A sanctimonious beast, I agree at the outset

parts.note: OK is said to show agreement, and here it comes at the start of the answer
pi, short for pious, means sanctimonious

explanation.surface: Someone agrees from the start about a self-righteous animal.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is informal British for priggishly pious. The okapi is an African forest animal related to the giraffe.
explanation.definitionFit: A giraffe relative from central Africa is an animal.

clue.text: Lawyer-cum-politician is rather wet!

parts.note: DA, district attorney, is an American lawyer
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: Someone both lawyer and politician is called a bit feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rather wet' suggests a feeble person, but here it means slightly moist.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly moist is damp, not soaking.

clue.text: Study a number and win

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
to earn is to win or gain by effort

explanation.surface: A pupil works on a sum and gets it right.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire knowledge through study is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Even so, the speed is immaterial

definitions.meaning: a phrase meaning nevertheless or anyway
read literally, travelling at whatever pace you like

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off how fast they must go.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the idiom meaning anyway or in any case, and literally at whatever pace or velocity.

clue.text: Medical man aids the troop on the move

indicators.note: the letters of these words are moving about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor helps a unit of soldiers as they march.
explanation.definitionFit: A bone and joint specialist is a kind of doctor.
